Final categorization: POSSIBLE  
(Justification: The paper is a non-review research article that uses land use modeling to project future forest area changes in New Zealand under multiple Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs). While it includes national-scale spatial implementation (NZFARM model operates at Territorial Authority level covering all of New Zealand) and compares ≥2 future scenarios quantitatively, its primary objective is not LULC prediction per se but rather assessing economic and environmental impacts—especially carbon sequestration, timber production, and water quality—under different socio-economic futures. LULC change (specifically planted forest expansion) is an endogenous outcome of the model used to derive these impacts, not the central research question. The study does produce quantitative estimates of forest area change over time and includes mapped regional results (e.g., Figure 6), but lacks explicit spatial accuracy metrics (e.g., validation against observed data, classification accuracy) typically associated with dedicated LULC prediction studies. Thus, LULC prediction serves as an intermediate step rather than the primary focus, meeting the definition of 'POSSIBLE'.)
